newsitem.title: USA: Nabisco earns $103 million in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Nabisco earns $103 million in quarter.

text.p: Nabisco Holdings Corp. said Monday it earned $103 million in its second quarter, up from a loss of $216 million a year earlier when the company took a one-time restructuring charge of $438 million.

Nabisco, maker of such products as Oreo and Chips Ahoy cookies, Ritz crackers, Grey Poupon mustard and other snacks and condiments, said excluding the year-earlier charge for restructuring, the company's income increased by 13 percent.

Nabisco said it earned $103 million, or 38 cents a share, on sales of $1.87 billion. Including the one-time restructuring charge, Nabisco lost $216 million, or 81 cents a share, on sales of $1.89 billion, in the same period of 1996.
The company said overall domestic sales increased by 1 percent during the quarter, and international sales increased by 2 percent.
Its biscuit unit, which includes Oreo and Chips Ahoy cookies, posted a 22 percent increase in operating income.

In its foods division, Nabisco said it posted a strong increase in sales of its Planters peanuts and Icebreakers gum, but those were offset by weakness in table spreads such as margarine and A.1. steak sauce.

However, operating income from Nabisco's international unit was down 19 percent to $51 million, due primarily to operations in Latin America, most notably in Brazil, where the poor results reflected a difficult economy, fierce competitiveness in the milk and biscuit categories and large inventory reductions by grocery wholesalers.
International earnings also were reduced by the costs of expansion in fast-growing Asian markets, particularly in China and Indonesia, Nabisco said.
Nabisco's stock traded at $37.875 cents, down 56 cents, in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

"Our results for the quarter were in line with our expectations and we remain confident that both our fundamental strategies and structure are sound," said H. John Greeniaus, chairman and chief executive officer of Nabisco Holdings Corp.

Key drivers of the earnings increase for the second quarter were strong growth in several snack categories, notably core biscuit products, nuts and confections, and dramatic cost and productivity improvements stemming primarily from the 1996 restructuring, Nabisco said.

"While sales were weak for some domestic products and the performance of our Brazilian businesses was very disappointing, the vast majority of our businesses are in solid shape and should respond well to the more aggressive marketing programmes that are planned for the second half of the year."
